news.title: Why half of England's World Cup defenders are on the move
news.lede: Will Djed Spence (left) and Ezri Konsa (middle) be the next England players to be involved in transfers this summer? England came third in this summer's World Cup - their best performance in a men's competition in 60 years - and now their players are in demand in the transfer market. Of the 27 players that went out to North America - 26 in the original squad and Trevoh Chalobah, who replaced the injured Tino Livramento - seven have moved clubs this summer, with another two linked with transfers. Morgan Rogers went from Aston Villa to Chelsea in a £117m deal, midfielder Elliot Anderson moved for £116m from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City and winger Anthony Gordon cost Barcelona almost £70m when transferring from Newcastle.

news.title: Jamaica takes major step toward historic 2031 Women’s World Cup role
news.lede: Jamaica has moved another decisive step toward becoming the first Caribbean nation to host matches at a FIFA Women’s World Cup after the Government and Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) formally signed the guarantee agreements required for the country’s participation in the 2031 tournament. Minister of Sport Olivia Grange and JFF President Michael Ricketts signed the documents Tuesday at the ministry’s offices on Trafalgar Road in St Andrew, strengthening the framework for Jamaica to work alongside FIFA and fellow co-hosts the United States, Costa Rica and Mexico. The agreement marks a significant transition from ambition to preparation, with Jamaica now formally committing to the obligations attached to staging World Cup matches. Legal and operational framework takes shape.

news.title: Republic of Ireland: Pairc Ui Chaoimh to host Women's World Cup play-off with Kazakhstan
news.lede: The Republic of Ireland have a 100% winning record at Pairc Ui Chaoimh in Cork. The home leg of the Republic of Ireland's 2027 Women's World Cup play-off with Kazakhstan will be played at Pairc Ui Chaoimh in Cork. Carla Ward's side travel to Kazakhstan on 9 October before the return fixture at the home of Gaelic games in Cork on Tuesday, 13 October. The winner of the first round play-off will face either Belgium or Poland for a place in the World Cup in Brazil next summer.

news.title: The Premier League Looks to Score World Cup Audiences With US Campaign
news.lede: Fans still suffering from the post-World Cup blues can rejoice! Top-tier soccer will soon be gracing our screens with the return of another season of the English Premier League. The season kicks off on Friday, August 21, pitting Arsenal against the other 19 teams as they look to defend their long-sought-after crown. Coming off a wildly successful World Cup, the league is hoping its players, including Erling Haaland, and its storylines can replicate the excitement from the tournament.

news.title: Can Infantino survive as half of FIFA's confederations turn against him?
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino is facing growing resistance from three of world football's six continental confederations as the 2027 presidential race draws closer, putting both his electoral support and his authority inside the organization under renewed pressure. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), and Concacaf, which oversee football in Europe, Asia, and North and Central America and the Caribbean, sharply stepped up their confrontation with FIFA on Monday. In a joint statement, they accused FIFA's leadership of a "fundamental breach of trust" and "deception" over the handling of an abandoned proposal to sell a stake in the FIFA World Cup to private investors. The three confederations rejected the idea that the dispute could be put down simply to poor communication or procedural mistakes.

news.title: Infantino Receives Support From 6 Arab Federations Amid Revolt Over World Cup Plan
news.lede: Zurich: The heads of six Arab football federations expressed their "full support" and "confidence" in Gianni Infantino on Thursday as the embattled FIFA president fights to keep his job after his failed World Cup private investment plan.The backing came from 2030 World Cup co-host Morocco, Qatar, Egypt, Mauritania, Lebanon and Sudan, with four of the signatories being FIFA council members." We, the undersigned leaders of our respective football associations, express our full support for Mr Gianni Infantino, President of FIFA, and reaffirm our confidence in his leadership and continued commitment to the development of football worldwide," the statement read." We deeply appreciate Mr Infantino's sustained efforts to advance football globally, expand opportunities across all regions and strengthen the game's role in bringing people and communities together."

news.title: South Korea's Football Assoc. Bribed International Referees With Escorts In The Early 2010s: Report
news.lede: The KFA has apologized for bribing refs with escort services. The Korea Football Association has issued a public apology after it was reported that it had bribed referees with escort services in the early 2010s. South Korea has qualified for 11 straight World Cups since 1986. According to a government report that was recently made public, the Korea Football Association (KFA) spent approximately $3,950 (5.6 million Korean won) on sexual services for foreign referees on eight separate occasions surrounding World Cup and Olympic qualifying matches between 2011 and 2012.

news.title: Former Man Utd star and World Cup winner joins Zinedine Zidane's new France set-up in shock selection
news.lede: FABIEN BARTHEZ has linked back up with old pal Zinedine Zidane after being handed a surprise role with France. The former Manchester United keeper, 55, has been named as Les Bleus’ new goalkeeping coach. France officially unveiled Zidane’s brand new backroom team on Thursday morning after he replaced Didier Deschamps in the top job. And Barthez is one of the standout names joining the Real Madrid legend as France look ahead to Euro 2028 in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.
